logline: A young couple inherits a crumbling English country house haunted by ghosts from every era of British history - and after a near-death accident, the new owner discovers she can see and hear them all.

renewal.note: Five series and Christmas specials concluded with the Series 5 Christmas special on 25 December 2023. The ensemble cast confirmed the show's conclusion. An American adaptation ran on CBS from 2021.

bollymeter.basis: An 87% Rotten Tomatoes score from 15 critics and an 81 Metacritic score for the series overall - The Observer called the show 'an exquisite exemplar of British comedy rep theatre' while The Guardian praised its rare warmth and wit.

pull_quotes.text: What an exquisite exemplar of British comedy rep theatre Ghosts has been.
Television has grown very tense in recent years, but there is a lot to be said for TV that is sweet, funny, clever and warm.

seasons.review_body: Series 1 of Ghosts aired on BBC One in April-May 2019, created by and starring the ensemble (Martha Howe-Douglas, Mathew Baynton, Simon Farnaby, among others), and quickly earned an 87% Rotten Tomatoes score. The Guardian praised it as 'sweet, funny, clever and warm' at a time when British prestige TV had grown relentlessly dark. The Independent found it 'sweet, but with a little edge'. The core premise - a historical cross-section of British society haunting a single house, from a medieval knight to a 1980s Tory MP - gave the writers a structural device of almost inexhaustible comic potential. Charlotte Ritchie and Kiell Smith-Bynoe as the living couple provided grounded emotional anchors for the ensemble's more baroque period characters. Critics noted the show's light touch on its absurd premise, treating the ghosts with genuine character depth rather than pure punchline.

bollymeter.basis: Critics and audiences maintained consistent enthusiasm as the show deepened its ensemble characterisation - the format's generosity of spirit held steady through a pandemic-disrupted production year.

seasons.review_body: Series 2 aired in September-October 2020, produced during the pandemic year, and maintained the affectionate critical standing the debut had established. Radio Times noted the show's ability to keep audiences on the 'Button House rollercoaster' without diminishing returns. The ensemble format proved remarkably robust - each ghost character's historical period opened fresh comedic territory, and the writers used the second series to develop the more emotionally complex backstories that distinguished the show from pure sitcom. The Metacritic series score of 81 reflects a critical consensus that held across the run. Fan enthusiasm grew steadily, and the show's gentle but precise satirical edge - particularly in the handling of the Tory politician ghost Captain and the World War Two soldier Pat - drew repeated critical appreciation.
seasons.season_over_season: Consistent with the debut's quality - the ensemble deepens rather than strains the premise.

bollymeter.basis: The show consolidated its reputation as one of the most reliably warm and inventive comedies on British television, with the ensemble's comfort in the roles generating increasingly sophisticated character comedy.

seasons.review_body: Series 3 aired in August-September 2021 as Ghosts had become one of BBC One's most beloved ensemble comedies. The writers' skill in developing emotional arcs within a premise-driven sitcom had grown more assured - the backstories of individual ghosts, particularly the medieval peasants and the Romantic-era poet Thomas Thorne, became generators of genuine feeling rather than just historical comedy. The American adaptation's launch in 2021 on CBS brought the British original renewed attention internationally, with the UK version's richer character texture drawing clear comparisons to its advantage.
seasons.season_over_season: The ensemble at full maturity - the character work grows more ambitious without losing the lightness of touch.

bollymeter.basis: Series 4 delivered the show's most emotionally ambitious character resolutions yet, with critical praise for the long-game payoffs built across four series of careful ensemble development.

seasons.review_body: Series 4 aired September-October 2022 and delivered the emotional payoffs the show had been carefully building across its run. Ghosts had by this point achieved something unusual in British sitcom - a consistent tonal signature across four series that never grew stale, because the ensemble's historical range kept providing new comedic terrain. The show's commitment to treating its ghost characters' existential situations - trapped in one house across centuries - with occasional genuine poignancy had by Series 4 produced some of the most memorable character moments of the entire run.
seasons.season_over_season: The most emotionally resonant series yet - four series of relationship building pays dividends.

bollymeter.basis: The final series earned the warmest critical send-off - The Observer's 'exquisite exemplar of British comedy rep theatre' tribute capturing the consensus that the show had become one of the most consistent BBC comedies in years.

pull_quotes.text: Ghosts is sweet, but with a little edge, the special effects unobtrusively done.

seasons.review_body: Series 5, airing October-November 2023 and concluding with a Christmas special on 25 December 2023, was received with widespread affection as the show's farewell. Critics who had followed Ghosts from the beginning found the finale series handled with the same lightness of touch and quiet emotional intelligence that had defined the run. The Observer's retrospective verdict - 'exquisite exemplar of British comedy rep theatre' - captured a critical consensus that the show had been something genuinely distinctive: an ensemble comedy that never needed to escalate or shock to retain audience affection. The Christmas special provided satisfying closures for individual ghost characters, with The Independent noting the show's 'sweet but with a little edge' quality holding to the very last.
seasons.season_over_season: A fitting conclusion - the finale series delivers emotional resolution without sacrificing the lightness that made the show special.
